option_description: All human and non-human privileged credentials (admin passwords, root/DB keys, service-account secrets, API keys, SSH keys, tokens) are stored only in a central encrypted vault and fetched at runtime, with no standing copies held in apps, files, or operator hands.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "credential_vaulting_rotation_and_secrets_management" — fires when privileged_credentials_vaulted is true — mitigating valid-account abuse and credential theft (ATT&CK T1078/T1555, MITRE M1026 Privileged Account Management). With credentials held only in the vault there are no human-held standing secrets to steal or dump.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the PAM vault account inventory (e.g. CyberArk Safes/Accounts list, HashiCorp Vault secret engine mounts, Azure Key Vault / AWS Secrets Manager inventory) and confirm it covers every class of privileged account — domain admin, local admin, root, DB, network device, cloud root/IAM. Confirm no privileged credential is documented or distributed outside the vault.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM console > Accounts/Safes inventory (CyberArk PVWA), or `vault secrets list` / Key Vault > Secrets
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Vault inventory shows coverage of all classes of privileged account (domain admin, local admin, root, DB, network device, cloud root/IAM); confirm no privileged credential is documented or distributed outside the vault.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Validate the vault's encryption standard at rest and in transit, and that retrieving a credential is gated by an approval / time-bound workflow rather than freely readable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Vault encryption standard validated (AES-256 or equivalent) at rest and TLS in transit; access to retrieve a credential gated by approval/time-bound workflow.

option_description: Automatic credential rotation runs on a recurring cycle, including rotate-after-checkin / one-time-use handling for the highest-value accounts.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "credential_vaulting_rotation_and_secrets_management" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when credential_rotation_enforced is true. Shortens the useful life of any captured secret, blunting OS credential dumping and password-store theft (ATT&CK T1003/T1555, M1027).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Pull the vault's rotation logs/policy (CyberArk CPM platform policy, Vault rotation/static-roles config, cloud Secrets Manager rotation schedule) and confirm every managed credential rotated within the policy interval and that rotate-after-use (one-time-use) is enabled so a checked-out password is invalidated on check-in.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM console > Platform Management / rotation policy and CPM rotation logs
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rotation logs show every managed credential rotated within the policy interval; confirm rotate-after-use is enabled so a checked-out password is invalidated on check-in.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm rotate-after-checkin / one-time-use is configured specifically for the highest-value accounts (domain admin, cloud root) rather than only the schedule-based rotation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: High-value account platform shows exclusive-use / one-time-password / rotate-on-checkin enabled; checkout returns a credential invalidated immediately on release.

option_description: Maximum number of days a privileged credential may remain valid before automatic rotation; a hardened configuration keeps this within a 30-90 day window (<= 90).
security_impact: Feeds the countermeasure "credential_vaulting_rotation_and_secrets_management" — the rotation-interval condition is satisfied when credential_rotation_max_days <= 90. A bounded interval caps how long a stolen secret stays useful (ATT&CK T1003/T1555, M1027).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured rotation interval on each managed-account platform (CyberArk platform `Rotation/MinValidityPeriod` and change frequency, Vault `rotation_period` / `max_ttl`, cloud Secrets Manager rotation interval) and record the longest interval in force across privileged platforms.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM console > Platform Management > rotation/change-frequency setting (or `vault read <mount>/config`)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configured maximum rotation interval is a number of days; secure when at or below 90. Map the read value directly to the integer day count.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check the rotation logs to confirm the configured interval is actually enforced (no credentials older than the stated maximum).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rotation history shows no managed credential exceeding the configured interval, confirming the stated max-days is real and enforced.

option_description: No privileged credentials or secrets are hardcoded in source code or configuration files; secrets are resolved from the vault at runtime.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "credential_vaulting_rotation_and_secrets_management" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when secrets_in_secret_manager_not_repo is true. Closes the hardcoded-secret path adversaries harvest from password stores and code (ATT&CK T1555, M1026).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan repository history and config/IaC/image layers for embedded secrets; any live hit indicates a hardcoded-secret gap the control must close.
how_to_obtain.command: git log -p | grep -Ei 'aws_secret|api[_-]?key|password|BEGIN (RSA|OPENSSH) PRIVATE KEY' ; trufflehog filesystem .
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No live secrets found embedded in repository history or config files; any hit indicates a hardcoded-secret gap the control must close.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the secrets inventory covers all microservices/service accounts, rotation logs meet the minimum rotation frequency, and access to each secret is audited and restricted to named principals (applications fetch at runtime).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secrets inventory covers all microservices/service accounts; rotation logs confirm every secret meets minimum rotation frequency; access to each secret is audited and restricted to named principals.

option_description: Encryption algorithm/strength protecting vault contents at rest; the secure state is AES_256. Enum: AES_256 | AES_128 | NONE.
security_impact: Feeds the countermeasure "credential_vaulting_rotation_and_secrets_management" — the at-rest-encryption condition is satisfied when vault_at_rest_encryption_strength == AES_256. Strong at-rest encryption protects the consolidated secret store from offline theft (M1026).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the vault's at-rest encryption configuration and map it to the enum: CyberArk Vault server uses AES-256 for the metadata/object store (confirm in the FIPS/encryption settings); HashiCorp Vault seal uses AES-256-GCM (`vault status` / seal config); cloud Key Vault / Secrets Manager report the KMS key spec. If AES-256 → AES_256; AES-128 → AES_128; no/absent at-rest encryption → NONE.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Vault server encryption/FIPS settings, or `vault status` (seal type) / KMS key spec in cloud console
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Vault encryption standard validated (AES-256 or equivalent) at rest and TLS in transit; access to retrieve a credential gated by approval/time-bound workflow. Map AES-256 → AES_256, AES-128 → AES_128, none → NONE.

option_description: Elevated privileges are granted just-in-time for a bounded task window and auto-revoked at task end/timeout, and no identity holds permanent membership in highly-privileged groups (Domain Admins, root, cloud Owner).
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "just_in_time_zero_standing_privilege_elevation" — the load-bearing trigger — firing when no_standing_admin_privileges_jit_required is true. Eliminates the standing-admin surface that escalation/abuse depends on (ATT&CK T1548/T1078, M1026/M1018).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review elevation request logs (Azure PIM activation history, CyberArk JIT/ad-hoc access, Vault dynamic-secret leases): confirm each grant carries start/end timestamps and an approval, and test that privileges auto-revoke at session end and that expired/unused elevations are denied.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure AD PIM > Privileged access > activation history, or PAM JIT elevation logs
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Review elevation request logs: each grant has a start/end timestamp and an approval; test that privileges auto-revoke at session end and that unused/expired elevations are denied.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate current membership of highly-privileged groups outside any active JIT window and confirm no human account holds persistent membership.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AD `Get-ADGroupMember 'Domain Admins'`, cloud IAM Owner/Admin role assignments
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm no persistent membership in highly-privileged groups (Domain Admins, root, cloud Owner/Admin) for human accounts outside an active JIT window.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6 Least Privilege

option_description: Maximum lifetime in hours of a granted just-in-time elevation before automatic revocation; a bounded window (<= 4h) caps how long an elevated session can be abused.
security_impact: Feeds the countermeasure "just_in_time_zero_standing_privilege_elevation" — the window condition is satisfied when max_elevation_window_hours <= 4. A short window limits the abuse value of any hijacked elevated session (ATT&CK T1134/T1548).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured maximum elevation lifetime in the JIT policy (Azure PIM role setting 'Maximum activation duration', CyberArk JIT session duration, Vault lease `max_ttl`). Record the value in hours.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure AD PIM > Roles > Role settings > Activation > Maximum duration, or PAM JIT policy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configured maximum elevation duration shown in hours; secure when at or below 4 hours. Map the read value to the integer hour count.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm via elevation logs that grants actually auto-revoke at or before the configured maximum (no session outlives the stated window).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Elevation activation history shows every grant de-escalated at or before the configured maximum, confirming the window is enforced.

option_description: Eligibility for privileged-access elevation is periodically recertified (e.g. quarterly) so stale entitlements are removed, and standing grants auto-revoke on expiry.
security_impact: Satisfies two countermeasures — "just_in_time_zero_standing_privilege_elevation" and "governed_approval_workflow_with_separation_and_break_glass_dual_control" — firing when periodic_privilege_recertification is true. Trims privilege creep so the JIT eligibility set stays least-privilege (ATT&CK T1548, M1018).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review access-review certifications (Azure AD Access Reviews, CyberArk/SailPoint recertification campaigns) for timeliness and confirm AC-6(7)-style periodic review reassigns or removes privileges no longer justified.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure AD > Identity Governance > Access reviews (or IGA recertification campaign records)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm AC-6(7) periodic review of assigned privileges with reassignment/removal where no longer justified; review access-review certifications for timeliness.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6 Least Privilege

how_to_obtain.instruction: Compare permissions assigned vs. permissions actually used (PAM entitlement analysis) and confirm over-provisioned rights are trimmed; confirm standing grants auto-revoke on expiry.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Compare permissions assigned vs. permissions actually used (PAM entitlement analysis) and confirm over-provisioned rights are trimmed.

option_description: All RDP/SSH/DB/cloud-CLI admin access is proxied through a central PAM gateway/jump host enforcing protocol and command filtering, AND direct-to-target admin network paths are blocked by segmentation so the broker cannot be bypassed.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "non_bypassable_session_brokering_with_phishing_resistant_mfa" — firing when bastion_mediates_all_admin_access is true. A non-bypassable broker forces every privileged session through policy/MFA enforcement (ATT&CK T1078, M1026).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt a direct admin connection to a target while bypassing the broker; confirm it is denied because firewall/segmentation permits only the broker as source. Inspect the gateway rules per protocol.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Attempt a direct admin connection to a target bypassing the broker; confirm it is denied (firewall/segmentation only permits the broker as source). Inspect gateway rules per protocol.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm MFA is required at the broker entry point before any session is brokered and that command/protocol policy is enforced (run a prohibited-command test and confirm it is blocked).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm MFA is required at the broker entry point before any session is brokered and that command/protocol policy is enforced (prohibited-command test blocked).

option_description: The broker requires phishing-resistant MFA (PIV/FIDO2/WebAuthn at AAL2/AAL3) bound per-user before any session begins, with no SMS/OTP/push fallback permitted.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "non_bypassable_session_brokering_with_phishing_resistant_mfa" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when phishing_resistant_authenticator_required is true. Defeats AiTM/token-replay downgrade on privileged login (ATT&CK T1078/T1134, M1032).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt broker access without valid MFA and confirm denial; confirm weak authenticators (SMS/OTP) are rejected or require a documented exception; check the MFA device inventory matches the active privileged-user population.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IdP/broker authentication policy (e.g. Azure AD Conditional Access authentication-strength = phishing-resistant MFA) and registered-authenticator report
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Attempt broker access without valid MFA and confirm denial; confirm weak authenticators (SMS/OTP) are rejected or require documented exception; MFA device inventory matches the active privileged-user population.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm MFA for all administrative access accounts uses phishing-resistant authenticators bound to AAL2/AAL3 (CIS Control 6.5, NIST 800-63B).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: MFA for ALL administrative access accounts confirmed (CIS Control 6.5) using phishing-resistant authenticators bound to AAL2/AAL3 per NIST 800-63B.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 6 — Access Control Management

option_description: Every privileged grant requires a formal request with business justification routed through a tiered approval workflow before access is provisioned, and access auto-revokes on expiry.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "governed_approval_workflow_with_separation_and_break_glass_dual_control" — firing when provisioning_requires_approval is true. An enforced request-and-approve gate prevents ungoverned standing access (ATT&CK T1078/T1548, M1026/M1018).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Sample recent access requests; confirm each has documented justification, an approver with appropriate authority, and that expired approvals auto-revoke. Confirm denied requests remain in the audit trail.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM/IGA request workflow records (Azure PIM approval history, ServiceNow access request tickets)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Sample recent access requests; confirm each has documented justification, an approver with appropriate authority, and that expired approvals auto-revoke. Denied requests remain in the audit trail.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the workflow is enforced (not advisory) — that access cannot be provisioned outside it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No path exists to provision privileged access bypassing the workflow; all grants trace to a recorded approval.

option_description: Separation of duties is enforced on the approval path per AC-5: the requester cannot approve their own privileged grant, and the security-admin role is separated from the audit role.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "governed_approval_workflow_with_separation_and_break_glass_dual_control" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when segregation_of_duties_enforced is true. Prevents single-actor abuse of the approval path (NIST AC-5, M1026).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm separation of duties: the requester/approver split is enforced (workflow rejects self-approval) and that security personnel administering access control do not also administer the audit function (AC-5).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Workflow approval-policy configuration and audit-admin role assignments
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm separation of duties: the requester/approver split and that security personnel administering access control do not also administer the audit function (AC-5).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-5 Separation of Duties

how_to_obtain.instruction: Test a self-approval attempt in the workflow and confirm it is rejected.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The workflow blocks a requester from approving their own grant; approval and oversight responsibilities sit with distinct principals.

option_description: Emergency break-glass access is pre-defined, requires dual-control (two-person) activation, fires immediate alerts on use, is fully recorded, and mandates post-use review.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "governed_approval_workflow_with_separation_and_break_glass_dual_control" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when break_glass_dual_control_enforced is true. Converts ungoverned shared emergency credentials into a governed, auditable path (ATT&CK T1078.001, M1026).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm break-glass accounts exist with credentials secured in the vault; test that activation requires two authorized administrators and immediately notifies security/audit. Review a recent activation for justification plus follow-up review.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM break-glass safe / emergency-access policy and activation alert records
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm break-glass accounts exist with credentials secured in the vault; test that activation requires two authorized administrators and immediately notifies security/audit. Review a recent activation for justification + follow-up review.

option_description: Maximum lifetime in hours of a break-glass emergency access grant before it auto-expires; a short, bounded window (e.g. <= 4h) is the secure state.
security_impact: Feeds the countermeasure "governed_approval_workflow_with_separation_and_break_glass_dual_control" — the break-glass-window condition is satisfied when break_glass_max_window_hours <= 4. A short auto-expiry stops emergency access becoming a silent persistent backdoor (ATT&CK T1078.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured break-glass grant lifetime in the emergency-access policy and confirm it auto-expires. Record the value in hours.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM emergency-access / break-glass policy > session or grant duration setting
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configured break-glass grant lifetime shown in hours; secure when it auto-expires at or below 4 hours. Map the read value to the integer hour count.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review a recent break-glass activation and confirm the grant was actually terminated at or before the configured window.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Break-glass activation record shows the grant auto-expired at or before the configured maximum window.

option_description: Privileged actions run only from dedicated, individually-attributable admin accounts — never the operator's daily-use account and never a shared/generic admin account — so every privileged action maps to exactly one identifiable human.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "dedicated_attributable_admin_accounts_with_discovery_and_dormant_disablement" — firing when dedicated_attributable_admin_accounts_enforced is true. Makes every privileged action attributable and removes shared-credential abuse (ATT&CK T1078.002, M1026/M1018).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm admin accounts are distinct from primary/daily accounts (AC-6(2)) and restricted to defined personnel (AC-6(5)); confirm no shared privileged credentials exist (each maps to one identity).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Directory account inventory — separate -adm/-admin account naming, and shared-account review
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm admin accounts are distinct from primary accounts (AC-6(2)) and restricted to defined personnel (AC-6(5)); confirm no shared privileged credentials (each maps to one identity).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6 Least Privilege

how_to_obtain.instruction: Validate against CIS Control 5.4 — administrator privileges restricted to dedicated administrator accounts; general computing performed from the non-privileged primary account.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Validate against CIS Control 5.4 — administrator privileges restricted to dedicated administrator accounts; general computing performed from the non-privileged primary account.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 5 — Account Management

option_description: All privileged and service accounts across Windows/Unix/DB/cloud/network estates are auto-discovered at least monthly, with newly-created privileged accounts detected within 24-48h, surfacing rogue or orphaned admin accounts.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "dedicated_attributable_admin_accounts_with_discovery_and_dormant_disablement" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when service_account_inventory_governed is true. Surfaces rogue/orphaned privileged accounts used for persistence (ATT&CK T1098, M1018).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the latest discovery scan and inventory; confirm coverage of all platform types and that newly-created privileged accounts are detected within 24-48h, with orphaned/rogue accounts carrying remediation plans.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM discovery module results (CyberArk Accounts Discovery, Delinea Discovery) / scan schedule
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Review latest discovery scan and inventory; confirm coverage of all platform types and that newly-created privileged accounts are detected within 24-48h; orphaned/rogue accounts have remediation plans.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm AC-2(7) privileged accounts administered under a role scheme with monitored assignments, and that an inventory of all admin (CIS 5.1) and service accounts (CIS 5.5) is maintained.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm AC-2(7): privileged accounts administered under a role scheme, role assignments monitored, and revoked when no longer appropriate; maintain an inventory of all accounts incl. admin (CIS 5.1) and service accounts (CIS 5.5).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2 Account Management

option_description: Maximum bounded inactivity window, in days, after which a dormant privileged account is auto-disabled; secure when <= 45 days.
security_impact: Feeds the countermeasure "dedicated_attributable_admin_accounts_with_discovery_and_dormant_disablement" — the dormant-window condition is satisfied when dormant_account_disable_window_days <= 45. A bounded window stops dormant accounts persisting as latent footholds (ATT&CK T1098, M1018).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured dormant-account auto-disable threshold (directory inactivity policy / PAM dormant-account rule) and confirm it is enforced by automation. Record the value in days.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Directory/PAM inactivity-disable policy setting (AC-2(3) automation)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configured dormant auto-disable threshold shown in days; secure when at or below 45 days and enforced by automation. Map the read value to the integer day count.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2 Account Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: Validate AC-2(3) automatic disable of expired/orphaned/inactive accounts and CIS 5.3 disable of dormant accounts after 45 days; confirm via sample that inactive accounts were actually disabled within the window.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Validate AC-2(3) automatic disable of expired/orphaned/inactive accounts and CIS 5.3 disable dormant accounts after 45 days.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2 Account Management

option_description: Privileged access for a departing person is revoked same-day on departure, closing the gap where an offboarded human's admin account could be retained or hijacked for persistence.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "dedicated_attributable_admin_accounts_with_discovery_and_dormant_disablement" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when offboarding_credential_revocation_enforced is true. Removes the post-departure orphaned-admin persistence path (ATT&CK T1098, M1018).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Sample recent separations and confirm privileged access was revoked within 24h (same-day); confirm dormant accounts auto-disable per policy and that revoked accounts remain in audit history (not deleted).
how_to_obtain.navigation: HR/IGA joiner-mover-leaver records vs. directory disable timestamps
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Sample recent separations and confirm privileged access revoked within 24h; confirm dormant accounts auto-disable per policy and revoked accounts remain in audit history (not deleted).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the offboarding procedure ties departure events to automatic same-day privileged-access revocation (PS-4/PS-5).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Offboarding workflow links HR departure to same-day revocation of all privileged access for the departing person.

option_description: Every privileged session is fully recorded (screen, keystroke, and command capture) so privileged activity is reconstructable and non-repudiable.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "tamper_evident_privileged_session_recording_audit_logging_and_anomaly_monitoring" — firing when privileged_access_via_pam_with_session_recording is true. Makes privileged activity reconstructable, supporting detection of account manipulation (ATT&CK T1098, M1047).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Retrieve sample session recordings from the PAM broker and confirm completeness (screen/keystroke/command); verify recordings are signed/encrypted and stored where the recorded admin cannot alter or delete them.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM session monitoring/recordings store (CyberArk PSM recordings, Delinea session monitoring)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Retrieve sample recordings and confirm completeness; verify recordings are signed/encrypted and stored where the recorded admin cannot alter or delete them.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm AU-9-style protection: session records stored on a physically separate system, write-once or cryptographically integrity-protected, with recording administration restricted to users distinct from those recorded.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm AU-9-style protection: audit/session records stored on a physically separate system, write-once or cryptographically integrity-protected, with audit management restricted to a subset of users distinct from those audited.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU family — AU-9 Protection of Audit Information

option_description: Every privileged action is logged with full context to centralized, externally-stored audit logs that the recorded admin cannot alter or delete (AU-9 separation of audit administration from the audited).
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "tamper_evident_privileged_session_recording_audit_logging_and_anomaly_monitoring" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when identity_access_audit_logging_enabled is true. Non-repudiable centralized logging detects/attributes account manipulation (ATT&CK T1098, M1047).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request recent privileged-activity logs; confirm all required fields (identity, source, resource, action, outcome, timestamp) are populated and that logs are forwarded to protected external storage (SIEM), signed/immutable, retained >=90d, and reviewed with documented findings.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM privileged-activity index (e.g. Splunk/Sentinel) and forwarding config
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Request recent privileged-activity logs; confirm all required fields populated and that logs are forwarded to protected external storage (SIEM), signed/immutable, retained >=90d, and reviewed with documented findings.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm AC-6(9) logs execution of privileged functions and AU-9(2) stores records on a physically different system so a compromise of the audited host cannot erase the only copy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm AC-6(9) logs execution of privileged functions and AU-9(2) stores records on a physically different system so a compromise of the audited host cannot erase the only copy.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6 Least Privilege

option_description: Privileged audit/session logs are signed or otherwise immutable (WORM, hash-chained, or equivalent) so any alteration or deletion is detectable, preserving non-repudiation of privileged misuse.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "tamper_evident_privileged_session_recording_audit_logging_and_anomaly_monitoring" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when audit_log_tamper_evident is true. Tamper-evidence preserves non-repudiation of privileged misuse (NIST AU-9, M1047).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify privileged audit and session logs are signed/immutable (WORM bucket, hash-chained, or cryptographic integrity protection) so any tampering is detectable; confirm administration of the log store is separated from the audited admins.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Log-store immutability settings (S3 Object Lock / WORM, SIEM signing) and store-admin roles
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Privileged audit and session logs are signed/immutable (WORM, hash-chained, or equivalent) so tampering is detectable.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU family — AU-9 Protection of Audit Information

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt (in a test) to alter or delete a recorded session/log entry and confirm the change is rejected or detectable via the integrity mechanism.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Modification/deletion of a stored log entry is blocked or flagged by the WORM/hash-chain integrity mechanism.

option_description: Retention period in days for privileged session recordings and audit logs; >= 90 days ensures sufficient history for forensic reconstruction and persistence detection.
security_impact: Feeds the countermeasure "tamper_evident_privileged_session_recording_audit_logging_and_anomaly_monitoring" — the retention condition is satisfied when log_retention_days >= 90. Sufficient history enables forensic reconstruction of slow-burn account-manipulation persistence (ATT&CK T1098, M1047).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured retention for privileged session recordings and audit logs (SIEM index retention, PAM recording-store retention policy, S3 lifecycle/Object Lock duration). Record the value in days.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM index retention settings and PAM recording-store/S3 lifecycle policy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configured retention for privileged session recordings and audit logs shown in days; secure when at or above 90 days. Map the read value to the integer day count.

option_description: Privileged sessions/accounts are monitored in real time for atypical usage (off-hours activity, mass account creation, unusual targets) with alerting, detecting account-manipulation persistence.
security_impact: Satisfies the countermeasure "tamper_evident_privileged_session_recording_audit_logging_and_anomaly_monitoring" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when privileged_session_anomaly_monitoring is true. Real-time anomaly alerting detects account-manipulation persistence as it happens (ATT&CK T1098, NIST SI-4/AC-2(12)).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm AC-2(12) monitors accounts for atypical usage and reports it; test that alert rules fire on policy violations such as privilege escalation outside business hours or mass account creation.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM/UEBA detection rules over privileged accounts (Sentinel/Splunk ES correlation searches)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm AC-2(12) monitors accounts for atypical usage and reports it; test that alert rules fire on policy violations (e.g. privilege escalation outside business hours, mass account creation).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2 Account Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the alert history to confirm anomaly rules are active and have actually fired/been triaged, not merely defined.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Alert history shows privileged-session anomaly rules firing and being triaged, confirming real-time monitoring is operational.

option_description: Minimum TLS protocol version negotiated on connections to the PAM broker and between broker and vault. Enum: SSLv3 | TLS1.0 | TLS1.1 | TLS1.2 | TLS1.3. Secure when TLS1.2 or TLS1.3 (SSLv3 and early-TLS disabled).
security_impact: Feeds the countermeasure "hardened_broker_transport_tls" — the TLS-version condition is satisfied when min_tls_version is in [TLS1.2, TLS1.3]. Disabling SSLv3/early-TLS prevents on-path downgrade and interception of brokered credentials (NIST SP 800-52r2).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the protocol versions the broker (and the broker-to-vault endpoint) will negotiate and take the lowest one offered as the value; map it to the enum (e.g. lowest accepted = TLS 1.2 → TLS1.2, TLS 1.3 → TLS1.3, any SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1 still accepted → that lower enum value).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLS 1.2/1.3 with FIPS-approved ECDHE+AEAD suites offered; no SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1 or NULL/RC4/CBC-only suites. Set the enum to the lowest version still negotiated.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 — Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of TLS Implementations

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check with testssl.sh or an openssl handshake forcing each legacy version to confirm SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1 are refused on the broker transport.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Legacy protocol probes (SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1) are refused; only TLS1.2/TLS1.3 complete a handshake, confirming the minimum-version enum value.

option_description: Interpreted boolean: true when only strong AEAD cipher suites with ECDHE forward secrecy are permitted and weak suites (NULL/RC4/MD5/export/CBC-only) are disabled on the broker transport.
security_impact: Feeds the countermeasure "hardened_broker_transport_tls" — the cipher condition is satisfied when cipher_suites_strong_only is true. Forward-secret AEAD-only ciphers prevent interception/downgrade of brokered credentials (NIST SP 800-52r2).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the cipher suites the broker offers and interpret as true only when AEAD+ECDHE forward-secrecy suites are exclusively permitted and weak suites (NULL/RC4/MD5/export/CBC-only) are disabled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLS 1.2/1.3 with FIPS-approved ECDHE+AEAD suites offered; no SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1 or NULL/RC4/CBC-only suites. true only if every offered suite is ECDHE+AEAD.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 — Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of TLS Implementations

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm with testssl.sh that no weak/forbidden cipher categories appear in the broker's offered suites.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: testssl.sh reports no weak ciphers (NULL/RC4/EXPORT/DES/3DES/CBC-only) and forward secrecy on all suites — interpret as true; any weak-cipher finding makes it false.

option_description: The broker and broker-to-vault TLS endpoints present and validate server certificates (chain, hostname, expiry), preventing an adjacent attacker from impersonating the broker or vault on the brokered session.
security_impact: Feeds the countermeasure "hardened_broker_transport_tls" — the certificate-validation condition is satisfied when server_certificate_validated is true. Validated certs stop broker/vault impersonation on the brokered session (NIST SP 800-52r2).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the certificate the broker presents and confirm the chain, hostname, and expiry are validated rather than skipped; also confirm broker-to-vault TLS clients do not disable verification (no insecure/skip-verify flags).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Broker presents a valid CA-chained certificate matching its hostname with a current validity window; broker-to-vault client config performs full verification (no skip-verify).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 — Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of TLS Implementations

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the broker and broker-to-vault TLS client configuration for any setting that disables certificate verification.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Broker TLS client config / vault connection settings (e.g. tls_skip_verify, insecure flags)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No certificate-verification-disabling flag is set; the broker validates the server certificate chain, hostname, and expiry on every connection.
